p: a: He vouches his apostleship (not for Titus, but for the Cretian's sake) both by the testimony of his outward calling, and by his consent in which he agrees with all the elect from the beginning of the world.
servant of God: A minister, as Christ himself, in his office of minister and head of the Prophets, is called a servant; Isa 43:10.
elect: Of those whom God has chosen.

and the acknowledging of the truth: The faith in which all the elect agree, is the true and sincere knowledge of God for this purpose, that worshipping God correctly, they may at length obtain everlasting life according to the promise of God, who is true, which promise was exhibited in Christ in due time according to his eternal purpose.
hope of eternal life: Hope is the end of faith.
promised before the: Freely and only from his generosity.
world began: See Geneva "2Ti 1:9"
But hath in due times manifested: This truth is not to be sought anywhere else, but in the preaching of the apostles.
Saviour: This word "Saviour" does not only signify a preserver of life, but also a giver of life.

To Titus: The apostle exhorts the Cretians to hear Titus, by setting forth his consent and agreement with them in the faith, and in addition shows by what special note we may distinguish true ministers from false.
Grace: There is but one way of salvation, common both to the pastor and the flock.
For this cause left I thee: The first admonition: to ordain elders in every church.
unruly: This word is used of horses and oxen, who will not tolerate the yoke.
For a bishop must be blameless: The second admonition: what faults pastors (whom he referred to before under the word elders) ought to be void of, and what virtues they ought to have.
steward of God: Whom the Lord has appointed steward of his gifts.
selfwilled: Not stubborn and hard to please.
sober: Cautious, and of a sound judgment, and of a singular example of moderation.
Holding fast the faithful word as: The third admonition: the pastor must hold fast that doctrine which the apostles delivered, and pertains to salvation, leaving behind all curious and vain matters.

that he may be able by: The fourth admonition: to apply the knowledge of true doctrine to use, which consists in two things, that is, in governing those who show themselves able to learn, and confuting the obstinate.

For there are many unruly and: An applying of the general proposition to a particular: the Cretians above all others need sharp reprehensions: both because their minds are naturally given to lies and slothfulness, and because of certain covetous Jews, who under a pretence of godliness, partly combined certain vain traditions, and partly old ceremonies with the Gospel.
circumcision: Of the Jews, or rather of those Jews who went about to join Christ and the Law.
One of themselves: Epimenides, who was considered a prophet amongst them. See Laertius, and Cicero in his first book of divination.
sharply: Clearly and plainly, and do not go about the bush with them.

Unto the pure all things are: He shows in few words, that purity consists not in any external worship, and that which is according to the old Law (as indifference of meats, and washings, and other such things which are abolished) but in the mind and conscience. And whoever teaches otherwise, does not know what true religion really is, and also is not to be heeded.
mind and conscience is defiled: If our minds and consciences are unclean, what cleanness is there in us before regeneration?
